reasoning: Failure-driven edits (Group 1) are kept in full: the bare-list-of-real-names replacement, the strip-what-the-clue-states bullet (highest support), the self-echo check, the part/organ decoy rule, and the person-name-form rule with its explicit tie-breaker. The tie-breaker says Rule 3 verbatim answers and the 'Sir' rule win, which protects stable passes such as Eisenhower and Hardy. They address slot-type and form-mismatch mechanisms, which are the persistent failure classes. Group 2 (success) edits cover patterns the failure edits do not touch, so I kept them: translation direction, the leading host-parenthetical as filler, the year-colon caption, archive-spam and quoted-epithet handling, members-to-parent clues, and quoted head versus quoted modifier. The last one resolves a collision with the delete-clue-words test. I added a short 'Rule 3 verbatim overrides' clause to the variant-name bullet so it cannot conflict with the archive-copy rule or with Group 1's name-form rule. No edit targets text between the SLOW_UPDATE markers, and none weakens Rule 3. Each edit stays short and conditional on a visible clue feature, with no gold answers embedded.

edits.target: If the list is of real people, answer with the team, state or other entity they share.
edits.content: - BARE LIST OF REAL NAMES (names only, no verb, or two people who held the same kind of post) asks for the ONE entity they share, never a listed person: senators/governors/mayors -> the state or city; kings/presidents/prime ministers -> the country; athletes -> team or country; band members -> the band. Find the place or group the passages put beside EVERY name and give its bare common name ('Spain', not 'Kingdom of Spain'). Write 'SLOT = ...' in your reasoning line first.

edits.target: ## Rule 4: Exact-match formatting of the final answer
edits.content: - STRIP WHAT THE CLUE ALREADY STATES (apply before every answer): when the clue says 'this island / river / city / magazine / airline / company', answer the bare proper name WITHOUT that word ('this island' -> 'Capri', not 'Capri Island'; 'this ride-hailing company' -> 'Uber', not 'Uber Technologies'), even if passages print the long form. The same goes for a place, campus or branch the clue already names ('this state university at Superior' -> 'the University of Wisconsin', not '...-Superior'; 'this bank's Dallas branch' -> the parent bank). If any descriptor or place word from the clue appears in your answer, delete it. Keep an extra word only when it is inseparable from the name (Salt Lake City, Dead Sea) or the head-noun exception below applies.

edits.target: ## Rule 2: Answer the referent, not a word from the clue
edits.content: - SELF-ECHO CHECK: if your answer (or its singular/plural stem) is a word already in the clue, it is almost surely wrong. Ask what DIFFERENT term the clue defines. (a) 'one of these <noun>s' after descriptors wants a compound ending in that noun that fits every descriptor ('pothole', 'sinkhole'), never the place named in the clue. (b) A bare definition clue with no 'this' ('Someone who cannot sleep') wants the standard dictionary/thesaurus term: find the passage that glosses the definition's words with a term and copy it with its internal hyphens, never the clue's own key word.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - 'this part / organ / piece / component of <thing>' asks for the physical PART itself (leaves, root, valve), not the process or technical term the passages keep repeating (transpiration, evaporation); that repeated topic word is usually a decoy. Ask 'which part does this?' and name it in the form the passages use.

edits.target: - Put only the bare answer in the answer tags. Do not write a sentence, restate the clue, or add dates, qualifiers or alternatives. Brief reasoning belongs before the tags.
edits.content: - PERSON NAME FORM (only when the clue asks for a person and no verbatim archive answer exists): use the form the passages' titles and headlines most often use, including a popular nickname form ('Jimmy', 'Ted', 'Bill'); do not expand it to a formal given name taken from a rank or biography line. Rule 3 verbatim answers and the knighted-'Sir' rule override this. Never use it to answer a bare list of names.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - A passage that only REPEATS the clue with no answer after it (video or quiz-spam titles, forum questions, crossword-solver listings) is not an archive hit. Skip it and take the answer from topical passages that paraphrase the clue's facts, or from your own knowledge if the passages are only noise. If the clue is a quoted epithet attributed to a source ('X magazine called him "King of ..."'), search the passages for the same quoted phrase next to a name ('<Name>, "king of ..."'). That name is the answer and the publication is an anchor.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Translation clues: the clue sets the direction. If it gives the foreign word or title and asks for English ('translates to this in English'), copy the English gloss printed beside it in the passages ('Title (English gloss)'), in full and in the passage's wording. Do not re-translate it, shorten it, or answer with the foreign phrase. If it gives the English meaning and asks for the name ('means "union"', 'is Latin for ...'), answer with the original-language name itself, bare, with no plural or type word.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - A parenthetical at the START of the clue that describes the host, video or Clue Crew ('(Jimmy of the Clue Crew grapples with another clue...)') is filler. Match archive lines on the clue text AFTER it. Only a TRAILING role-and-dates parenthetical is a caption (see Strategic guidance, section 2).

edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content: - A year followed by a colon and a role ('1968:Starring Barbra Streisand', '1994:Directed by X') is a caption. It asks for the work (film, album, book, show) from that year tied to that person. Pick the title the passages pair with BOTH the year and the person, and answer with the title alone, not the person or the year.

edits.target: Never cut a part that identifies the person: keep the regnal numeral of a king or of a play's title character ('Richard III', not 'Richard'; 'Henry V').
edits.content: - VARIANT NAMES: when passages give several forms of the same entity (native vs. Anglicized spelling, original vs. translated film title, Charley/Charlie), answer with the one repeated most across passages and used in the sentence that matches the clue. Do not mix forms or invent a 'more correct' spelling. A verbatim archive answer (Rule 3) overrides this.

edits.target: the answer is exactly one of the listed options, copied verbatim. Use the context to pick which.
edits.content: - 'X & Y are varieties / examples / kinds of this <category>' ('Vermont & Tillamook are American varieties of this cheese'): the clue names MEMBERS and asks for the single PARENT that the passages list all of them under (Cheddar). Never answer with one of the named members. Give the bare parent word.

edits.target: - A word in quotation marks inside the clue (a 'drag', a nickname) is usually a pun or hint tied to the answer. Look for passages where that word appears next to a candidate and answer with that candidate.
edits.content: - QUOTED HEAD vs QUOTED MODIFIER: ask which half of the standard compound the clue supplies. If the quoted word is the HEAD ('cools to this "point"'), the bare modifier alone is not the answer. Give the full compound as the passages repeat it ('dew point'); the delete-clue-words test does not apply. If the quoted word is the MODIFIER already given ('A "hasty" dessert'), answer only the missing head ('pudding').
